A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 31 pages of each version, including Algorithms 1–2, Figure 1, equations and Appendices A–E, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical bounds and proofs. Appendix A derives values analytically for a Tiger POMDP example; no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v3 retains the theoretical analysis and analytical Tiger POMDP example, without adding original empirical or simulation outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same temporal-difference updates, linear critics, log-linear policy and natural-gradient estimation procedure. The pseudocode edits only change punctuation.

E1.justification: Neither version reports training or evaluation datasets. The analytically studied POMDP setting and Appendix A's Tiger example are unchanged.

E2.justification: The symmetric algorithm from Cayci et al. (2024) remains the analytical comparator. Neither version reports an empirical baseline comparison.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocol is introduced or revised. The sampling assumptions and algorithmic step-size prescriptions are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A retains the same Tiger POMDP aliasing example and analysis. No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses or additional case studies are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The corrected expectation in Appendix E concerns a theoretical derivation.

E6.justification: No empirical results are added, removed or revised. Appendix A's closed-form value functions and aliasing finding are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D, equation (172), replaces v2's inconsistent expansion involving B and gamma with 2l, consistent with the existing definition of l. Appendix E, equation (261), adds an outer expectation over the initial agent state before equation (262). These correct local derivation steps; theorem statements and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: extending asymmetric actor-critic analysis to agent-state policies and explaining its benefits through removal of aliasing-related error terms.

C2.justification: The discussion retains the tradeoff between reduced aliasing error and potentially higher asymmetric gradient-approximation residuals. The fixed-agent-state and linear-approximation scope, variance caveat and future directions are unchanged.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, feature bounds, step sizes and discounted-visitation sampling instructions retain the same technical information. No implementation details or code/data access information are added.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to earlier asymmetric learning and finite-time actor-critic analyses are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the sampling-assumption wording on page 4, standardizes capitalization in Theorems 1–2, removes the duplicated 'if' in Appendix A and adjusts punctuation. Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There is limited text reflow around Figure 1 and local realignment of the corrected Appendix D equation block. Figure 1 and Algorithms 1–2 retain their structure and placement; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The corrections to equations (172) and (261) resolve local inconsistencies in substituting l and averaging over initial states, improving mathematical precision and proof traceability. These are limited gains; the main theorems, algorithms and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
